A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIRReS, with matching core methods, benchmarks, and experiments despite the changed title and format. All pages, including supplementary figures and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original geometry, material, relighting, and novel-view experiments on TensoIR and OWL, together with component ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results in Tables 2–3, ablations in Table 4 and Appendix B.3, and per-scene qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the described material-network output from five channels, including metallic, to four channels for albedo and roughness. v3 specifies metallic as an additional channel for OWL. The two-stage reconstruction, joint rendering losses, reservoir sampling, and multi-bounce tracing remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four TensoIR scenes and four OWL scenes, covering geometry, material decomposition, novel-view synthesis, and relighting. Synthetic novel-view examples remain in the supplementary figures despite removal of their aggregate scores.

E2.justification: The evaluated baselines remain NVdiffrec-MC, TensoIR, and GS-IR in the benchmark comparisons. The per-scene comparator selections are also retained. Newly cited denoising and specular-reconstruction works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The reported environment-map resolution changes from 128×256 to 256×512. v3 also specifies dataset-provided NeuS meshes for OWL initialization, qualifying v1's general NeuS2 setup. Metrics, the default 32 samples per pixel, and reported training time remain unchanged. These revised descriptions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The reservoir/multi-bounce ablation in Table 4 is retained. The indirect-illumination, sample-count, and radiance-field-rendering studies in Figures 7–9 move to Appendix B.3 without changed evidence. The geometry-related failure examples in Figure 10 are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging benchmark metrics over test images remains unchanged. Discussion of Monte Carlo rendering variance concerns the method, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 removes Table 2's synthetic novel-view PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS entries, including MIRReS's 35.260 PSNR and GS-IR's 35.333. The remaining Table 2 values and all values in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. Figure 6 replaces novel-view renderings with relighting examples.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a mathematical specification of the denoiser, including edge-dependent weights and normalized filtering in Eqs. 17–21. The core rendering integrals, Monte Carlo/RIS estimators, and loss equations remain mathematically equivalent despite consolidation and notation changes. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: joint explicit geometry/material/lighting recovery, physically based multi-bounce illumination, reservoir-based acceleration, and strong decomposition and relighting performance.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1's discussion acknowledging similar synthetic novel-view performance to TensoIR and GS-IR and attributing it to baked-in lighting. Appendix C adds a specific future direction combining MIRReS with specular-reflection methods. The limitations involving initial geometry and detached non-primary-ray gradients remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands previously sparse implementation information: hash-grid configuration, network depths and widths, the three-iteration edge-aware denoiser, and streaming reservoir updates and reuse. Existing visibility and regularization details are relocated rather than newly introduced. However, v1's explicit choice of the power heuristic over the balance heuristic is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting denoising and weighted reservoir sampling, plus specular-reconstruction approaches in future work. The bibliography drops NeFII, Ref-NeRF, and PBRT. The main positioning against implicit, mesh, and Gaussian representations, including the multi-bounce novelty claim, remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, methods, experiments, and conclusion are rewritten. Technical details, supplementary experiments, and limitations are organized into Appendices A–C, with revised subsection structure and expanded explanations and captions. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column conference format, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Figure 5 is rearranged, Figure 6 substitutes relighting panels, Table 2 loses its novel-view columns, and equations gain visual annotations. Figures 7–10 move into appendices; the per-scene grids are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the core implementation easier to understand and reproduce through explicit network, denoising, and reservoir-reuse details and clearer organization. These gains outweigh a limited reporting loss: the synthetic novel-view scores and parity discussion disappear, along with the explicit MIS-heuristic choice. The retained benchmark and ablation results provide essentially the same empirical support, so the improvement is chiefly in documentation.
